checks: Read s261_q44_matched_fit.py: the data vector is what the summary says (Q29 s183 X961 2.2in h150 aperture 1-0, Q34 s192 12m+7m comb 3-2, Q29 s185_box pm150 13C). No Harada peak pixel enters, except CS, which is scaled by the aperture/Harada factor with +-25% added. That is correctly flagged as non-matched. AGREE that the mixed-aperture Q42 caveat is removed for the 4 12C + 2 13C lines.

Read analysis_q44.txt: the quoted N, S and Bridge numbers are the file's numbers. N P(Tk<=30) is 0.013-0.029 for the LN prior and 0.020-0.042 for the flat-logX prior when X<=100. Extending to X<=178 gives 0.04-0.05 for LN and 0.20 for flat. M12 (12C only) has P(cold)=0.40-0.49, BF 1. I did not re-run the fits (several hours). The reporting is consistent and honest about prior dependence, so I AGREE with the numbers as reported.

Re-derived the radial significance from s260f.txt. Core r<1.1 0.0339+-0.0055 vs ring 1.1-3.3 0.0184+-0.0062 is an independent pair: diff 0.0155+-0.0083 = 1.9 sigma. The nested 0.3 vs 3.3in value of 2.0 sigma is consistent. So the 'real radial decline of 13C/12C' is a ~2 sigma hint, for H13CN only 1.5 sigma. The report gives Q44c confidence 'medium' and writes 'a real radial decline'. That is too strong. A 2.2in taper also makes r<0.3in a beam-dominated pixel, not a resolved core. DISAGREE with 'medium' and with the wording 'is therefore an aperture effect'. The Harada-consistency part (0.037 vs 0.046, 1.1 sigma) is fine. That the drop is not a calibration offset follows from the within-line comparison, but the data cannot show how much of it is gradient and how much is noise.

Tension in the headline. The summary says X_N=66-77 is an aperture average of a gradient, and it sits at or above the top of the Tang/Martin 21-67 range. Q40 found X_N 31-35 with Harada peak pixels, which are core-weighted. The cold-branch verdict is therefore tied to which aperture is fitted. The 1-0 12C + 13C data alone give P(cold)=0.33, which equals the prior (M10, BF 1). The discrimination comes only from 3-2 12C plus the cross-band scale prior. This sits at the same level as the 12C-only prior effects that team-a (p0044-r03) shows move P(Te>=50) from 0.67 to 0.24 as the band-scale sigma goes 0.10 to 0.25. With 20/25% priors and a flat X to 178 the result is P(cold)=0.20, BF 2. 'Disfavoured' is therefore not robust. 'Prior-dependent, 0.02-0.2' is the supported statement, and confidence should stay low.

Requested pieces: (a) radial test done (see above). (b) 1-0-only variant done (M10, M10C: no discrimination). (c) 12C 4-3 done only at the 4.1x2.7in beam, mismatched and 12C only. The 8-10 dchi2 from it depends on the band-7 +15% scale and on beam dilution not being modelled. It is a supplement only, and the summary correctly says so. M32 (3-2 12C + 13C 1-0 with no 1-0 12C) was NOT run. It is the cleanest test of whether the 12C 1-0 lines or the 3-2 lines drive the result, and it was in the plan.

fixes.what: Run M32 (and M3-only 12C control), at least for N, S and C with 10/15 and 20/25% band priors, and report P(cold) and dchi2(cold-hot) at fixed X.
fixes.why: The decision between branches hinges on 3-2 12C plus 13C 1-0. M32 isolates this and shows whether the 12C 1-0 lines and the cross-band scale prior are essential. M4 is not needed, since Q42 already showed H13CN 4-3 does not discriminate.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Run the same grid with lines=(1,3) plus iso. If the result is carried by the cross-band scale, say so and give the result for a free (flat) band scale ratio 1-0/3-2 within 30-40%.

fixes.what: Fit core and outer apertures jointly or separately: 12C 1-0 and 13C 1-0 at r<1.1in and the 1.1-3.3in ring, with 12C 3-2 at the same apertures from the Q34 12m+7m 2.2in cube. Alternatively run the aperture-averaged fit with X as two values (core, ring).
fixes.why: The gradient claim implies a one-zone aperture-mean X_N=66-77 is not the core X. The core-weighted Q40 value was 31-35. The cold-branch probability depends on this X, so a core-aperture fit with matched 3-2 (r<1.1in cuts at 2.2in) is the right test of whether the N conclusion changes.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Use annular spectra from the same tapered cubes with consistent, noise-correlation-aware errors (nested apertures: use the covariance, not independent noise; or ring-vs-core independent differences only).

fixes.what: Downgrade Q44c: confidence low, wording 'a ~2 sigma hint of a 13C/12C decline, not established'. Quote the independent core-vs-ring difference (1.9 sigma). State that r<0.3in at a 2.2in taper is a beam-dominated pixel.
fixes.why: 1.5-2 sigma on one line pair, with an HCN counterpart at 1.5 sigma, does not establish a gradient. It cannot support the sentence that the X_N is an aperture average of a thinner core.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Add a null test: the same core-vs-ring statistic at S and the Bridge (flat, as in the table) and a noise-injection estimate of the false-gradient rate.

fixes.what: Rewrite the Q44a/Q44b headline: the cold branch is prior-dependent (P(cold|N)=0.01-0.2; BF 2-60), the result is not 'disfavoured' in general, and the X_N 66-77 value is an aperture average that is above the starburst 12C/13C range and in tension with Q40. Add the two-zone case team-a studies (p0042, p0044-r03) as an acknowledged limitation, and state the CS-scaled variants (MC) are not matched and should not be quoted as the primary number.
fixes.why: The report quotes 0.0002-0.011 for MC in the same breath as the matched result. One non-matched input drives the lowest numbers.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Keep MC out of the primary table or label it explicitly. Quote the range across prior choices in the abstract line.

notes_for_questioner: (1) Check the X_N 66-77 value against an independent isotope ratio (13CO/C18O or 12CO/13CO ~11-15 in team-a p0039 with R=40-90). If X_N must be <~60, the one-zone fit is biased. (2) A two-zone (core+envelope) matched fit with X shared and all data at 2.2in, since the radial test and team-a p0042 both point to two components. (3) Is a 3-2 12C and 13C at <=1.1in obtainable from Xb4d tapered to 1.1in (13C 3-2 is not covered by tuning, so only 12C 3-2 at 1.1in versus 12C 1-0 at 2.2in)? That would give the core-only 12C part. (4) Publication: p0044's 'disfavoured' wording needs an update with the Q42/Q44 prior dependence, and X_S remains a lower bound.
